promise: A curated doorway to useful world resources. It names access, reuse, automation, and uncertainty separately; it never turns a free doorway into a claim of ownership, safety, truth, or unlimited service.

methodology.summary: Resources are selected for broad civic value, credible stewardship, a usable free path, and an official source that explains access or terms.
methodology.classification: Free to access, openly reusable, and safe to automate are different questions. Every card answers all three and keeps provider-specific limits visible.
methodology.maintenance: Each entry carries a checked date. Re-check the linked official terms before material, commercial, high-volume, medical, legal, or emergency use.
methodology.boundary: The Kingdom curates directions, not endorsements. Linked providers remain independent; their current terms, licences, privacy practices, coverage, and operational limits govern use.

privacy.human_surface: Search and filters run only inside the downloaded page. The page sends no query, creates no profile, and contacts a provider only when the visitor chooses a link.
privacy.machine_surface: The static catalog receives no need or query. A client may match locally. Calling a linked provider crosses into that provider's own privacy, quota, and terms boundary.

foundation.meaning: A broad first shelf chosen for civilisational usefulness, durable stewardship, legible terms, and a meaningful free path. Foundation is a starting order, not an objective ranking of worth.
criteria: knowledge or infrastructure many different communities can build from
credible public-interest stewardship and stable identifiers or provenance
a meaningful free path rather than a short promotional trial
download, bulk, API, or offline routes where the resource can responsibly offer them
access, reuse, automation, uncertainty, and safety can be stated separately

categories.label: Knowledge & evidence
categories.description: Structured facts, scholarly provenance, and research discovery.

categories.label: Learning
categories.description: Books, courses, and educational foundations that can be reached without tuition.

categories.label: Earth & place
categories.description: Maps, biodiversity, hazards, and the physical context shared by life.

categories.label: Public life & economy
categories.description: Official statistics, food systems, health context, and small-business registers.

categories.label: Rights & law
categories.description: Primary legal and rights sources for orientation, never a substitute for counsel.

categories.label: Resilience
categories.description: Humanitarian and hazard information for preparation, with local authorities kept primary.

categories.label: Digital safety
categories.description: Open vulnerability evidence, defensive guidance, and public-interest infrastructure.

categories.label: Culture & memory
categories.description: Public collections and cultural records with item-level rights kept visible.

kits.label: Trace a claim to evidence
kits.invitation: Resolve names and identifiers, find the scholarly trail, then read the source rather than inheriting a summary.
kits.boundary: Metadata can locate evidence; it cannot establish that a claim is true or that a paper is sound.
steps: Resolve the entity or DOI.
Compare independent indexes and references.
Open the primary source and retain its identifier, version, and licence.

kits.label: Learn a subject without tuition
kits.invitation: Begin with a structured course or textbook, then widen into literature and research.
kits.boundary: Free learning materials do not automatically include assessment, accreditation, tutoring, or commercial reuse rights.
steps: Choose a structured starting text.
Keep the edition and licence with any notes or adaptations.
Use research indexes to update claims that may have changed.

kits.label: Carry knowledge offline
kits.invitation: Prepare a small, local library that can remain useful through weak connectivity, high data costs, censorship, or disruption.
kits.boundary: Offline copies can be large, incomplete, or stale. Every source keeps its own licence, and a snapshot never replaces current local emergency, medical, or legal information.
steps: Choose the language, subject, device, and storage budget.
Check each file's date, size, provenance, and licence before downloading.
Test the library without a network and plan a gentle, explicit update rhythm.

kits.label: Understand a place
kits.invitation: Combine geography, public statistics, food systems, and biodiversity without flattening a place into one score.
kits.boundary: Coverage, borders, dates, definitions, and uncertainty differ. A map or indicator is one situated record, not the place itself.
steps: Start with the geographic scope and vintage.
Read each indicator's definition and source.
Retain attribution and record-level licences when combining data.

kits.label: Prepare for disruption
kits.invitation: Use global signals to build awareness, then return authority to current local warnings and people on the ground.
kits.boundary: These sources can be late, incomplete, estimated, or wrong. They must not independently trigger evacuation, medical, or other life-safety decisions.
steps: Check event time, review status, and source.
Confirm against the relevant local authority.
Use reports for preparation and context, not as live commands.

kits.label: Find rights and primary law
kits.invitation: Reach official instruments, recommendations, labour standards, and legislation before seeking jurisdiction-specific help.
kits.boundary: A source can orient and evidence; it cannot know the full facts, current local procedure, or give legal advice.
steps: Identify the jurisdiction, date, and issuing body.
Follow the identifier to the official text.
Check authenticity, amendments, applicability, and professional help where consequences are material.

kits.label: Protect a software project
kits.invitation: Find known vulnerable dependencies, raise exploited issues, and turn open guidance into release checks.
kits.boundary: Absence from a catalog is not proof of safety, and a passed checklist is not a security or compliance certification.
steps: Match exact package versions against OSV.
Prioritize matches also present in CISA KEV.
Apply relevant OWASP checks and keep transport certificates renewed.

kits.label: Visit cultural memory
kits.invitation: Search books, collections, biodiversity literature, and preserved source code while carrying provenance and rights with every object.
kits.boundary: Catalog access is not blanket permission over every image, object, person, mark, or work; rights remain item-specific.
steps: Open the item record before the media file.
Keep creator, institution, identifier, and rights statement.
Check local copyright and personality rights before reuse.

kits.label: Navigate a UK small-business question
kits.invitation: Ground a business question in official statistics, register facts, and current import measures before asking for consequential advice.
kits.boundary: Registers and statistics provide facts, not endorsement, credit judgment, tax classification, customs classification, or legal advice.
steps: Verify the entity and filing date.
Use a dated official statistic for context.
Check commodity, origin, destination, and measure details with a qualified human when money or liability turns on them.

resources.name: Wikidata
resources.provider: Wikimedia Foundation and the Wikidata community
resources.description: A multilingual, community-maintained knowledge graph with references, qualifiers, APIs, queries, and downloadable dumps.
good_for: Narrow factual discovery with visible references
resources.coverage: Global and multilingual; community coverage and sourcing vary by topic and place.

access.note: Public pages, query service, APIs, and dumps are available without payment; identified clients receive higher API tiers.

reuse.note: Structured Wikidata data is dedicated to the public domain; referenced source material keeps its own rights.

automation.limits: API tiers and concurrency limits apply; WDQS uses separate dynamic limits.
automation.note: Use a descriptive User-Agent, narrow live queries, cache, back off, and use dumps for bulk extraction.

resources.caveat: Community assertions are not automatically authoritative. Keep references and qualifiers, and do not infer sensitive identity attributes from gaps or graph proximity.

resources.name: Crossref REST API
resources.description: Public DOI and scholarly-work metadata for resolving citations, funders, publishers, relations, and provenance.
good_for: Resolving a DOI to canonical metadata
resources.coverage: Deposited metadata from Crossref members; completeness and field quality vary by depositor.

access.note: The public REST API needs no signup; a contact email opts requests into the polite pool.

reuse.license: Record and field specific
reuse.note: Bibliographic facts are broadly reusable, but deposited abstracts and other content may remain copyrighted.

automation.limits: Respect current rate-limit headers; public and polite pools have separate rates and concurrency limits.
automation.note: Identify the client, include mailto, cache results, and back off on 429 responses.

resources.caveat: A DOI record locates a work; it is not a quality judgment, and metadata can be incomplete or stale.

resources.name: OpenAlex
resources.description: A large scholarly graph connecting works, authors, institutions, topics, sources, and citations.
resources.coverage: Global scholarly metadata assembled algorithmically from many sources; entity matching and coverage are imperfect.

access.note: The API has a small anonymous budget and a larger daily free-key budget; quarterly snapshots are free to download.

reuse.license: CC0-1.0 dataset
reuse.note: OpenAlex presents the complete dataset as CC0; linked full text and source records retain their own rights.

automation.limits: API calls have query-dependent cost and daily credit budgets; the full snapshot is large.
automation.note: Use the snapshot for systematic analysis and the API for bounded discovery; retain canonical work identifiers.

resources.caveat: Do not mistake graph rank, citation count, or automated entity resolution for importance, identity, or truth. Full-text rights are separate.

resources.name: Europe PMC
resources.description: A biomedical literature index with citations, annotations, grants, and supported access to openly available full text.
resources.coverage: Life-science literature and related records; full-text availability and licences vary by article.

access.note: The REST API and supported bulk channels are publicly accessible.

reuse.license: Article and record specific
reuse.note: Metadata, abstracts, and full text do not share one blanket licence; retain each article's rights statement.

automation.limits: Use REST, OAI, or FTP channels and reasonable bounded requests.
automation.note: Do not crawl the human website; filter for open-access content and preserve article-level licences.

resources.caveat: Literature search is not diagnosis or medical advice. Check study design, publication status, date, and independent evidence.

resources.name: Software Heritage
resources.description: A long-term archive of publicly available source code, preserving exact files, releases, repository states, and provenance with durable SWHIDs.
good_for: Recovering public source and release history
Citing exact software artifacts with SWHIDs
resources.coverage: Public source code harvested from many forges and deposits; not every repository, branch, licence, or later deletion is captured immediately or completely.

access.note: Archive browsing and pointwise public API access are free; an optional account can receive higher API quotas.

reuse.license: Factual archive metadata is reusable; source artifacts retain upstream rights
reuse.note: Provenance and computed factual metadata may be used subject to privacy rules. Every archived file keeps its own copyright, licence, patent, and trademark obligations.

automation.limits: The public API is for point queries, save requests, and individual Vault bundles; mass extraction is not authorised through it and quotas can change.
automation.note: Use SWHIDs and documented APIs, cache point results, and arrange bulk access or a mirror for significant extraction.

resources.caveat: Archived code is unvetted and may be unsafe to execute. Developer names or emails may be present; profiling, solicitation, and privacy-harming reuse are forbidden. Automated licence detection is not legal assurance.

resources.name: OpenStax
resources.description: Peer-reviewed introductory textbooks available free on the web and as downloadable PDFs.
good_for: Foundational accounting, economics, statistics, and science
resources.coverage: More than 80 primarily introductory college and school titles; editions and regional fit vary.

access.note: Web and PDF books remain free, but some current chapter pages ask readers to sign in before continuing; access varies by page and format.

reuse.license: Usually CC BY-NC-SA for current and newly updated titles
reuse.note: OpenStax changed its default in 2026; verify the exact title and edition because some books retain earlier licences.

automation.limits: Current book pages prohibit using OpenStax content to train or ingest into large language models without permission; no bulk extraction API is offered.
automation.note: Link people to the exact title and edition. Keep attribution and the exact licence with any permitted human-led adaptation.

resources.caveat: Free access does not mean commercial reuse or AI ingestion is permitted, and a textbook edition may not reflect the newest research or local curriculum.

resources.name: MIT OpenCourseWare
resources.description: Course notes, syllabi, assignments, and selected media from thousands of MIT courses.
resources.coverage: A broad archive of MIT course materials; not every course has complete lectures, solutions, or current content.

access.note: Materials can be read and many courses downloaded without registration.

reuse.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, with exclusions
reuse.note: Attribution and share-alike apply; MIT names, marks, privacy/publicity rights, and third-party content are excluded.

automation.limits: Use offered course downloads rather than aggressive crawling.
automation.note: Retain course provenance, notices, and excluded-content markings.

resources.caveat: OCW offers materials, not enrolment, instructor access, credit, certification, or an MIT qualification.

resources.name: Project Gutenberg
resources.description: A long-running digital library of ebooks that are mostly in the United States public domain.
resources.coverage: Primarily older works cleared under United States copyright law; language and geographic coverage vary.

access.note: Ebooks and catalog feeds are available without an account.

reuse.license: Mostly US public domain; Project Gutenberg terms and trademark conditions also apply
reuse.note: Copyright can still subsist outside the United States, and individual items or formats can carry notices.

automation.limits: Automation should use supported mirrors, feeds, and bulk channels rather than scraping the main site.
automation.note: Follow the robot-access policy and keep item identifiers and notices.

resources.caveat: A work believed public domain in the United States may still be protected where the reader or reuser lives.

resources.name: Kiwix
resources.provider: Association Kiwix and independent content communities
resources.description: Open software and a multilingual ZIM catalog for carrying whole knowledge libraries on phones, computers, and local networks without a live internet connection.
good_for: Prepared access through censorship, high data cost, or disruption
resources.coverage: A multilingual catalog of independently sourced ZIM snapshots; language, topic, file size, update date, and source coverage vary by package.

access.note: Public readers, server software, catalog browsing, and community ZIM downloads need no paid account; optional hardware and custom services are separate.

reuse.license: GPL-3.0 software; source-specific ZIM content licences
reuse.note: Kiwix software is GPL-3.0, while every packaged library follows the licence and rights of its independent content source.

automation.limits: Catalog results are paginated and ZIM files can be very large; public mirrors remain shared infrastructure.
automation.note: Use the documented OPDS v2 catalog and official download mirrors, expose language, date, size, and licence before transfer, and do not create service accounts by bot.

resources.caveat: Offline snapshots can be old, incomplete, or too large for a device. Source accuracy and content rights remain separate, and a stored copy must not be mistaken for current emergency, medical, or legal information.

resources.name: OpenStreetMap
resources.description: A global, collaboratively maintained geographic database with extracts and a public editing ecosystem.
good_for: Self-hosted search, routing, and tiles built from extracts
resources.coverage: Global, with completeness, tagging, freshness, and local knowledge varying from place to place.

access.note: The database and planet extracts are public; community-hosted tiles and search services are scarce shared infrastructure, not unlimited APIs.

reuse.license: ODbL-1.0
reuse.note: Attribution is required and share-alike obligations can apply to derived databases.

automation.limits: Public Nominatim is at most one request per second; public tiles forbid bulk or offline scraping and have no SLA.
automation.note: Use extracts or self-hosted/provider services for production and high volume; identify clients and cache user-triggered lookups.

resources.caveat: Do not treat OSM alone as safety-critical routing, cadastral truth, an official address register, or a neutral settlement of disputed borders.

resources.name: Natural Earth
resources.description: Small, cartographer-made public-domain vector and raster datasets for world maps at several scales.
resources.coverage: Global and intentionally generalized for small-scale cartography.

access.note: Static downloads need no account, key, or hosted API.

reuse.license: Public domain
reuse.note: Commercial and noncommercial reuse is allowed; attribution is appreciated.

automation.limits: Download and cache the versioned static packages rather than repeatedly fetching them.
automation.note: Record dataset name, scale, and release date for reproducibility.

resources.caveat: Generalized geometry is not suitable for navigation, parcel boundaries, local analysis, or definitive legal borders.

resources.name: GBIF
resources.description: A global infrastructure for species, taxonomy, and biodiversity occurrence records contributed by many publishers.
resources.coverage: Global but uneven by species, location, time, institution, and collection effort.

access.note: Public search and GET APIs are open; asynchronous downloads require a free account.

reuse.license: Record-level CC0, CC BY, or CC BY-NC
reuse.note: Retain publisher, dataset, DOI, and the licence attached to each record or download.

automation.limits: API rates are dynamic and may return 429; use the download service for large occurrence sets.
automation.note: Cache taxonomy resolution and preserve download DOIs for reproducibility and attribution.

resources.caveat: Absence of records is not evidence of species absence. Coordinates can be uncertain or sensitive and need ecological and ethical review.

resources.name: Biodiversity Heritage Library
resources.description: A free digital library of biodiversity literature, illustrations, taxonomy, OCR, and collection metadata spanning centuries of recorded knowledge about life on Earth.
good_for: Bulk metadata, OCR, and literature discovery
resources.coverage: Global consortium collections across many centuries and languages; digitization, taxonomy, OCR quality, and item rights vary by volume and contributor.

access.note: Browsing and offered file downloads are free without an account; API v3 uses a free key while OAI and bulk exports provide other routes.

reuse.license: CC0 metadata; item-specific public-domain or Creative Commons content
reuse.note: BHL metadata is CC0. Scans, images, and OCR keep volume-level rights: much is US public domain, while in-copyright contributions are often CC BY-NC-SA.

automation.limits: Use API v3, OAI-PMH, or published bulk exports; API access requires a free key and service capacity is shared.
automation.note: Prefer monthly exports for corpus-scale work, retain holding institution and item rights, and record the retrieval date and source identifier.

resources.caveat: OCR, metadata, historical taxonomy, and recorded distributions can be wrong or outdated, and US public-domain status may not carry across borders. BHL completed a major infrastructure-host transition in June 2026; re-check availability before depending on live services.

resources.name: USGS Earthquake Hazards feeds
resources.description: Global real-time earthquake feeds and a query service with event time, magnitude, location, and review status.
good_for: Preparedness dashboards with official source links
resources.coverage: Global seismic events observed and reviewed by USGS and partner networks; small-event completeness varies.

access.note: Real-time GeoJSON feeds and FDSN queries require no key.

reuse.license: US government public-domain data, subject to source notices
reuse.note: Credit USGS and preserve source metadata and update status.

automation.limits: FDSN queries cap results at 20,000; 429 may apply and feeds are preferred for current events.
automation.note: Use the provided real-time feeds, cache briefly, and record event update and review status.

resources.caveat: Events can be revised. Never use this source alone as an evacuation trigger; follow current local emergency authorities.

resources.name: World Bank Indicators API
resources.description: Long-run national and global development indicators with definitions, sources, vintages, and programmatic access.
resources.coverage: Roughly 16,000 indicators across countries and aggregates; frequency, lag, and coverage differ by indicator.

access.note: The V2 Indicators API does not require an API key.

reuse.license: World Bank-produced open datasets generally CC BY 4.0; dataset-specific terms control
reuse.note: Some indicators incorporate third-party data or restrictions; inspect the dataset record.

automation.limits: No fixed numeric quota is published; paginate, cache, and avoid unbounded queries.
automation.note: Retain indicator code, definition, source organization, date, and retrieved vintage.

resources.caveat: Indicators are constructed measures, often lagged and revised. Do not turn them into simplistic rankings or real-time financial advice.

resources.name: FAOSTAT
resources.provider: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
resources.description: Global statistics on food, agriculture, land, trade, emissions, prices, and food security.
good_for: Country and commodity comparisons with official flags
resources.coverage: More than 245 countries and territories across many domains; observations may be reported, estimated, or imputed.

access.note: The web database is free; the new developer API uses an account-issued token.

reuse.license: CC BY 4.0 by default, with additional FAO database terms and third-party exceptions
reuse.note: The added terms restrict use connected to promoting a commercial enterprise, product, or service; attribution, non-misrepresentation, and item-specific notices also apply.

automation.limits: The new API does not publish one stable numeric quota; old endpoints should not be relied on.
automation.note: Use the current developer portal, cache responses, and preserve official status flags and dataset revision.

resources.caveat: Always preserve flags that distinguish official, estimated, and imputed values; different releases can revise the past.

resources.name: WHO Data
resources.description: Global public-health indicators, estimates, methodologies, and downloadable data from WHO programs.
resources.coverage: Global and national health indicators; availability, comparability, and estimation methods vary.

access.note: The data portal and offered downloads are public.

reuse.license: Generally CC BY 4.0 with WHO data terms and third-party exceptions
reuse.note: Additional conditions cover attribution, non-endorsement, non-de-anonymization, and third-party material.

automation.limits: The legacy GHO OData service was scheduled for retirement and successor API documentation remains in transition.
automation.note: Use current portal downloads and source links; do not hard-code the deprecated legacy endpoint.

resources.caveat: WHO estimates can differ from national figures. Show methodology and vintage, and never turn an indicator lookup into diagnosis or medical advice.

resources.name: Eurostat
resources.provider: Statistical Office of the European Union
resources.description: Official European statistics with APIs for datasets, structures, classifications, and geographic information.
resources.coverage: European Union, EEA, candidate, and partner geographies depending on dataset; latest API data can be revised.

access.note: Public data and APIs are available without an API key.

reuse.license: EU-owned statistical content generally CC BY 4.0; exceptions apply
reuse.note: Third-party material and some trade data can carry different conditions.

automation.limits: Services update regularly and expose current versions; large requests should be split and cached.
automation.note: Persist raw snapshots and dataset codes because later revisions can replace earlier values.

resources.caveat: Keep the dataset code, geography, unit, time, flags, and retrieval date; latest-value APIs are not revision archives.

resources.name: UK Office for National Statistics API
resources.description: Official UK economic, population, labour, price, and regional statistics through datasets and a public beta API.
resources.coverage: United Kingdom official statistics; dataset frequency, revision policy, and geographic detail vary.

access.note: The public API needs no key.

reuse.license: Open Government Licence where stated
reuse.note: Retain ONS attribution and inspect dataset notices for third-party content.

automation.limits: Published bot limits include 120 requests per 10 seconds and 200 per minute; the API is beta.
automation.note: Cache and pin dataset edition, version, dimensions, and retrieval timestamp.

resources.caveat: A beta interface may break, and an official statistic still needs its definition, revision status, and confidence information.

resources.name: Companies House API
resources.description: The official public register interface for UK company identity, filings, officers, and filing history.
resources.coverage: Companies registered in the United Kingdom; register data reflects submitted filings and statutory processes.

access.note: API access uses a free Companies House account and API key; the public register is free to search.

reuse.license: Register and field specific
reuse.note: Public availability is not blanket permission over every field or person; check Crown copyright, OGL, and personal-data duties.

automation.limits: Default limit is 600 requests per five minutes.
automation.note: Cache stable records, avoid unnecessary personal-data collection, and retain filing dates and source links.

resources.caveat: Registration is not endorsement, solvency, trustworthiness, beneficial-ownership certainty, or a substitute for due diligence.

resources.name: UK Trade Tariff APIs
resources.provider: UK Department for Business and Trade and HM Revenue & Customs
resources.description: Official commodity codes, duties, VAT, quotas, measures, and guidance for UK goods trade.
resources.coverage: Imports to and exports from the United Kingdom, dependent on commodity, origin, destination, date, and procedure.

access.note: The public service is free; developer keys are being introduced for authenticated rate-limit tiers.

reuse.license: UK government source and endpoint terms
reuse.note: Retain the official measure, legal base, date, and source; do not imply HMRC endorsement.

automation.limits: Further rate limiting is planned for Q4 2026; adopt the developer portal and keys rather than relying on anonymous behavior.
automation.note: Cache dated measures and require contextual review of classification, origin, valuation, and procedure.

resources.caveat: A search result is not a binding customs classification or tax answer. Consequential classifications need full facts and qualified review.

resources.name: Universal Human Rights Index
resources.provider: Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights
resources.description: A searchable index of recommendations and observations from UN human-rights mechanisms.
good_for: Finding recommendations by country, theme, or mechanism
Rights research with dates and provenance
resources.coverage: UN treaty bodies, special procedures, and Universal Periodic Review records; publication backlogs can occur.

access.note: The human index is free; API access is described through provider contact/onboarding.

reuse.license: OHCHR site terms and source-document rights; no single open dataset licence confirmed
reuse.note: UHRI's data page encourages sharing while its terms assert proprietary rights. Link or export for research, keep provenance, and confirm permission before wholesale republication.

automation.limits: No stable public rate limit is published and advertised export URLs were not reliable when checked.
automation.note: Use the human index now; automate only after OHCHR confirms a current endpoint and conditions.

resources.caveat: Recommendations are contextual official records, not allegations, verdicts, or inputs for automated country scoring.

resources.name: ILO NORMLEX
resources.description: Official information on international labour standards, ratifications, supervisory comments, and related national laws.
resources.coverage: ILO member states and international labour instruments; applicability depends on ratification, jurisdiction, and date.

access.note: The official NORMLEX search interface is publicly accessible.

reuse.license: ILO and document-specific terms
reuse.note: Public reading does not create a blanket redistribution licence; retain official document identifiers and notices.

automation.limits: No general public automation contract is cataloged here.
automation.note: Use the official human interface and source links; seek a documented data channel before systematic extraction.

resources.caveat: An instrument's existence does not establish that it is ratified, in force, directly applicable, or determinative in a particular dispute.

resources.name: EUR-Lex and CELLAR
resources.provider: Publications Office of the European Union
resources.description: Official European Union law discovery with persistent CELEX and ELI identifiers plus feeds, REST, and SPARQL access through CELLAR.
resources.coverage: European Union law and publications; consolidated texts, language versions, and legal effects must be checked carefully.

access.note: EUR-Lex and CELLAR public discovery and query channels are accessible without payment.

reuse.license: EU-owned content generally CC BY 4.0 unless marked; third-party rights remain
reuse.note: Only the Official Journal edition is legally authentic; retain identifiers, version, language, and source.

automation.limits: No single numeric public quota is promised; queries should be bounded, cached, and retried gently.
automation.note: Prefer persistent CELEX or ELI identifiers and record whether a text is original, amended, or consolidated.

resources.caveat: Legal texts require jurisdiction, date, amendments, authenticity, and applicability checks; this doorway is not legal advice.

resources.name: WIPO Lex
resources.description: A free global database of intellectual-property laws, treaties, judgments, and member profiles.
resources.coverage: Global intellectual-property source collection; completeness, translations, status, and legal effect vary.

access.note: Human search access is free.

reuse.license: WIPO Lex terms and source-specific rights
reuse.note: Noncommercial reproduction conditions and third-party/source rights apply; official texts remain controlling.

automation.limits: Automated queries and scraping are prohibited; the terms also cap rapid search activity.
automation.note: Link citizens to the human interface and never build an automated scraper against it.

resources.caveat: Database access is not legal advice, an official translation guarantee, or permission to automate the service.

resources.name: ReliefWeb
resources.provider: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
resources.description: A curated index of humanitarian reports, maps, assessments, jobs, and training from many organizations.
good_for: Following sources during preparedness and recovery
resources.coverage: Global humanitarian reporting; content is contributed by partners and can lag unfolding events.

access.note: The human service is public; API callers need a preapproved appname.

reuse.license: Partner and item specific
reuse.note: ReliefWeb indexes material from many publishers; link to reports and keep source, date, and item rights.

automation.limits: The API allows up to 1,000 entries per call and 1,000 calls per day for an approved appname.
automation.note: Use metadata and outbound source links rather than mirroring partner reports.

resources.caveat: Reports can be partial, delayed, or contested and do not replace local emergency instructions or direct community knowledge.

resources.name: Global Disaster Alert and Coordination System
resources.provider: United Nations and European Commission partners
resources.description: Global multi-hazard event awareness combining automated alerts, maps, and coordination information.
resources.coverage: Global earthquakes, floods, cyclones, volcanoes, droughts, and related events depending on source systems.

access.note: The public site and API can be read without payment or authentication.

reuse.license: GDACS attribution plus source-product rights
reuse.note: Credit GDACS and retain the licence and source attached to each underlying product.

automation.limits: Collections are paginated and no permanent numeric service quota is promised.
automation.note: Poll gently, deduplicate event identifiers, and store source time and update time.

resources.caveat: Alerts are automated or semi-automated and may be delayed or wrong. They never override national or local warnings.

resources.name: OSV.dev
resources.provider: Google Open Source Security team and advisory ecosystems
resources.description: An open vulnerability database and API that maps advisories to precise open-source package versions and commits.
resources.coverage: Open-source ecosystems and imported advisory databases; coverage depends on upstream publishers and package identifiers.

access.note: The public API currently needs no key and ecosystem dumps are available.

reuse.license: OSV service and upstream advisory-source licences
reuse.note: Preserve advisory aliases, source database, references, and upstream licence/provenance.

automation.limits: No current request rate limit is published; HTTP response-size limits apply and bulk dumps suit systematic scans.
automation.note: Batch package queries, cache advisory IDs, use dumps for fleet-wide checks, and back off on service errors.

resources.caveat: No match does not prove a dependency safe. Package identity, version ranges, reachability, and remediation still need verification.

resources.name: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog
resources.provider: United States Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency
resources.description: A focused public catalog of vulnerabilities with evidence of exploitation in the wild.
resources.coverage: A curated subset of known vulnerabilities that meet CISA's exploitation criteria; it is intentionally not comprehensive.

access.note: The catalog and JSON/CSV downloads are public and unauthenticated.

reuse.note: The catalog is offered under CC0; retain CISA as source and the catalog date for operational clarity.

automation.limits: Use the published static JSON or CSV and refresh on a bounded schedule.
automation.note: Join by CVE and record date added, due date, action, and ransomware-use fields without inventing risk scores.

resources.caveat: Not being listed does not mean a vulnerability is unexploited or low risk; combine KEV with broader advisory and asset context.

resources.name: OWASP Cheat Sheet Series
resources.description: Concise, open defensive guidance for common application-security decisions and implementation patterns.
resources.coverage: Application and platform security topics curated by the OWASP community; relevance and freshness vary by sheet.

access.note: The web series and source repository are public.

reuse.license: CC BY-SA 4.0
reuse.note: Attribution and share-alike apply to adapted content.

automation.limits: Clone or download the public repository for repeated local use rather than scraping pages.
automation.note: Pin the source revision and retain attribution when turning guidance into derived checklists.

resources.caveat: A checklist is guidance, not a threat model, penetration test, compliance audit, or certification.

resources.name: Let's Encrypt
resources.description: A free, automated, publicly trusted certificate authority for enabling HTTPS.
good_for: Reducing the cost barrier to HTTPS
resources.coverage: Eligible internet domain names under subscriber and validation requirements; it does not secure application code or private trust systems.

access.note: Certificates are issued without a fee through an ACME account key after domain-control validation.

reuse.license: Subscriber agreement and certificate-policy terms
reuse.note: This is a public service, not a reusable dataset licence; subscribers accept the current agreement.

automation.limits: An ACME account key, domain-control challenges, issuance rate limits, and the published certificate-lifetime schedule apply.
automation.note: Use an ACME client, protect the account key, automate renewal with margin, monitor failures, and stage bulk issuance changes.

resources.caveat: Issued certificates and domain names enter public Certificate Transparency logs, and issuance requests create service logs. A valid certificate protects transport and domain authentication; it does not prove that a site, claim, operator, or application is safe.

resources.name: Library of Congress API
resources.description: Public catalog and collection discovery across books, photographs, recordings, maps, manuscripts, and exhibitions.
resources.coverage: Library of Congress collections and described partner material; digitization and metadata completeness vary.

access.note: JSON and YAML API representations require no key.

reuse.license: Item-specific rights statements
reuse.note: The Library does not own all collection rights; carry the rights-and-access statement from each item.

automation.limits: The published limit is 20 requests per minute; excessive use can be temporarily blocked.
automation.note: Cache results, paginate gently, and store the canonical item URL and rights statement.

resources.caveat: A digitized item's visibility does not mean it is public domain or clear of privacy, publicity, cultural, or trademark concerns.

resources.name: Smithsonian Open Access
resources.description: Millions of collection records and media, with explicitly marked CC0 assets available for broad reuse.
good_for: Cultural and educational projects with provenance
resources.coverage: Smithsonian museums, research centers, libraries, archives, and the National Zoo; media and rights availability differ by item.

access.note: Human access is public; API access uses a free api.data.gov key.

reuse.license: CC0 only for assets explicitly designated Open Access
reuse.note: Non-CC0 items and privacy, publicity, trademark, cultural, and donor restrictions remain separate.

automation.limits: The API key normally carries an hourly quota; current bulk distribution should be preferred for systematic use.
automation.note: Filter on the Open Access designation and retain item ID, institution, title, creator, and source URL.

resources.caveat: Only assets explicitly marked CC0 carry the Open Access reuse grant; other legal and ethical rights can remain even for a CC0 file.

resources.name: Europeana
resources.provider: Europeana Foundation and contributing cultural institutions
resources.description: A multilingual discovery platform for digitized European cultural heritage from thousands of institutions.
good_for: Finding reusable heritage objects by rights label
resources.coverage: European galleries, libraries, archives, and museums; metadata and digital-object availability vary by contributor.

access.note: Human discovery is public; API use requires a free key and production projects can be reviewed.

reuse.license: Europeana metadata CC0; digital-object rights are item specific
reuse.note: Always retain and obey the rights statement attached to the linked object.

automation.limits: Reasonable-use limits apply and production access can be reviewed or constrained.
automation.note: Filter by rights statement, cache metadata, and link back to both Europeana and the contributing institution.

resources.caveat: CC0 metadata does not make the depicted or linked object CC0. Check every object's rights badge and originating record.
